claims.statement: UPS publishes a money-back guarantee for qualifying late deliveries, requires a timely claim with shipment details and allows account holders to request a refund through invoice dispute tooling.

contrary_evidence: Guarantees are service- and destination-specific and contain broad exclusions; carrier automation or suspensions can compress the recoverable pool.

structure.control_point: The deadline-aware eligibility engine and invoice-level proof that a carrier credit was received
structure.critical_dependency: Carrier guarantees must apply in the target services and account permissions must allow claim submission and credit reconciliation

thesis: Continuously compare promised delivery commitments with carrier scans and invoice lines for ecommerce merchants and 3PLs. When a shipment qualifies under the carrier's guarantee, submit the documented request within the deadline, track exclusions and match the carrier credit back to the invoice. Charge only on credited shipping charges and distribute through shipping software, WMS vendors and 3PLs; each carrier decision strengthens an exclusion and refund-outcome corpus.
